summary: Mesa County, CO stone observatory and shelter house on Grand Mesa built 1936-37; NRHP-listed 1997; building closed and boarded up as of 2022.

facts.design: One-story, T-shaped observatory of roughcut native basalt, built with a rim wall and latrine
facts.status_note: Building stands but was closed and boarded up as of 2022, per Wikipedia

access.note: Reached by Land's End Road from the Grand Mesa Scenic and Historic Byway; the road is about half paved and half gravel. Wikipedia says the observatory building was closed as of 2022.

events.note: Built 1936-37 by the Forest Service and WPA with help from two CCC side camps. A 1938 newspaper quoted on the Forest Lookouts page says the shelter house and lookout were completed during 1937.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on February 28, 1997, reference 97000124

notes_for_editor: Kind is the main question. Forest Lookouts calls the building a lookout and shelter house; Wikipedia calls it a ranger observatory; the NRHP nomination calls it an observatory and names visitor-center and concession uses. None of these sources describes a fire-detection role, so the brief's kind of unknown may need a non-tower type. Closure is as of 2022 per Wikipedia and should be checked. The Forest Lookouts Colorado index lists Lands End Point alphabetically but gives it no status row, so no FFLA status is used. Brief coordinates 39.0253, -108.2238 agree with Wikipedia's 39.025, -108.2236. Dates: 1936-37 per the register, Wikipedia and the sign; the 1938 newspaper says 1937, so the built event is recorded as 1936 with the range in the note. No photos added; Wikipedia's image credit and license were not checked.
